page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs using Ampere AmpereOne-M processors operating at a sustained clock speed of 3.6 GHz. Because each physical core executes exactly one hardware thread, the instance avoids resource contention and performance jitter typically associated with simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 32.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core.

This server type does not bundle local disk storage, meaning operating system disks and persistent application data must rely on external network-attached block volumes. Hardware accelerators and discrete GPUs are absent from this configuration. Network allocation includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the underlying hardware is 64-bit Arm, deployment targets must support the aarch64 instruction set, and software reliant on x86 vector extensions such as AVX is not compatible.

The dedicated core architecture provides consistent compute performance without noisy-neighbor interference on execution units. VM.Standard.A4.Flex.4-32 fits general-purpose workloads compiled for Arm, including microservice clusters, containerized application environments, web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and mid-tier application runtimes.
